chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Run-ins with the police
summary: His only arrest was at about nine in Decatur during a fire bell; he never had trouble over marijuana.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Jay C., a lot of the musicians have said to me, they used to get in trouble like with the police and things down South travelling. Did you ever get arrested or anything like that?

Musicians used to tell me that guys - it was easy for black musicians to go to jail for different things, like you're in a town or something, you know. Did you ever get arrested or anything like that?

No. Yeah, I got arrested in Decatur, Georgia. No, this was fun. You know we had the fire bells then. You know they have a large population now. So we were playing at night and there was a fire, so they rang the bell and we went up on the town to see which way the fire truck was going, three of us. Everybody ran but me and I was too stupid. I was too scared to run.
Oh, I think around about 9 years old.
You never had any other problems like with the police or government or anything like that?
No... I don't get fresh with no cops and I don't have no problems with nobody. Sometimes, you know if you're in
a crowd and they say keep moving or something like that - I'm going to move.
The cops never arrested musicians for smoking marijuana and stuff like that?
They didn't lock me up for marijuana; I don't smoke.
I wish they would, then I would sue the city.
No, never... The only two reefer I saw in 1929, were the two I told you I smoked with Louis Armstrong...
